extracted.intended_audience: authors seeking agent representation (adult fiction, YA, select middle grade, memoir, narrative nonfiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Agent Hillary Jacobson's wishlist and submission guidelines: the kinds of manuscripts she is actively building for (genres, themes, tone, examples) and how to submit a query (what to include and where).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively building a list consisting of commercial and literary fiction, YA, select middle grade, as well as narrative non-fiction and memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: 'actively building a list consisting of commercial and literary fiction, YA, select middle grade, as well as narrative non-fiction and memoir.' Use this as the primary genre filter when querying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional and intellectual impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reads widely and is on the hunt for any and all writing that provokes a strong emotional reaction, adds an important perspective to the cultural conversation or forces the reader to challenge what they think.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should provoke strong emotions, contribute to cultural conversation, or challenge reader assumptions. Prefer work that does one or more of these (ideally all).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of underrepresented voices and non-US settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Especially invested in promoting underrepresented voices and eager to read stories not set in the US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions from marginalized authors and stories set outside the U.S. are prioritized; agent expresses explicit interest in broadening represented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: dark and joyful range
rubrics_metrics.description: While she certainly is drawn to the very dark, she does love more joyful stories too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent is open to a wide tonal range—from very dark/unsettling to joyful—so match tone to the manuscript's strengths rather than forcing it into a single mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modern female experience / feminist themes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fiction or non-fiction that explores the unique burdens and pleasures of the modern female experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent lists Sally Rooney, Curtis Sittenfeld, Carmen Maria Machado and Meg Wolitzer as favorites. Also: 'In that vein, she wants to see anything that promotes, analyzes, or incorporates feminism.' Use topical relevance to contemporary female experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoirs with fiction-like plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoirs that read like tightly plotted and suspenseful fiction a la BRAIN ON FIRE, HOUSE IN THE SKY, EDUCATED or THE FACT OF A BODY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoirs should have strong narrative drive, tight plotting, and a sense of suspense or structure comparable to page-turning nonfiction memoirs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive, suspenseful true crime
rubrics_metrics.description: True crime that feels as immersive and suspenseful as the best thrillers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: SAY NOTHING, I'LL BE GONE IN THE DARK, RED NOTICE. True crime should read like a gripping narrative rather than dry reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspense / 'secrets & lies' novels
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspense, or what she likes to call 'secrets & lies' novels — gravitates toward the dark and disturbing and loves feeling unsettled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent cites THEN SHE WAS GONE, TANGERINE, THE PERFECT NANNY, ANATOMY OF A SCANDAL, WATCH ME DISAPPEAR, BITTERSWEET, TELL ME LIES, and Liane Moriarty. Aim for psychological suspense, unsettling atmosphere, and concealed truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for diverse perspectives in suspense and domestic fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: She’d especially love to see these stories told from diverse perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: THE EXPATRIATES, LITTLE FIRES EVERYWHERE, THE MOTHERS, BEHOLD THE DREAMERS, STAY WITH ME. Diverse narrators and cultural viewpoints increase interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twist endings / shocking revelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sucker for a truly shocking and mind-blowing twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent names I LET YOU GO and BEHIND HER EYES as touchstones. Well-executed, surprising twists that feel earned are highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction (near-real world with a twist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Speculative fiction that features a world like ours, but with a twist — the everyday with just a touch of the unreal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: THE IMMORTALISTS, STATION ELEVEN, THE AGE OF MIRACLES, PROVIDENCE, NEVER LET ME GO. Agent favors subtle speculative elements grounded in recognizable settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA — inventive, distinctive world-building
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA: incredibly inventive and distinctive world-building like in THE THOUSANDTH FLOOR, WARCROSS, or GRACELING.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YA fantasy/speculative submissions should show fresh, memorable worlds and mechanics that feel original and well-realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA contemporary — voice-driven
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA contemporary: 'Contemporary is all about the voice.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, distinct narrative voice is critical for YA contemporary novels. Agent references I AM NOT YOUR PERFECT MEXICAN DAUGHTER, THE HATE U GIVE, etc., as examples of voice-forward work.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA — high concept executed brilliantly
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA: 'High concept executed brilliantly' — compelling premise done well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ELSEWHERE, EVERY DAY, EVERYTHING, EVERYTHING. A striking central idea must be matched by excellent execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: YA historical with unique perspective / magical twist
rubrics_metrics.description: For YA: historical from unique perspectives and/or with a magical twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: THE GENTLEMAN’S GUIDE TO VICE AND VIRTUE, THE DIVINERS, PASSENGER. Historical settings should feel fresh, or combine history with speculative/magical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subversion of genre tropes
rubrics_metrics.description: Always a plus if you can subvert the tropes of the genre!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that plays with or upends established genre expectations is especially appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Own Voices preference
rubrics_metrics.description: #ownvoices!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit encouragement for authors telling stories from their own marginalized/underrepresented perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query even if outside guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes she surprises herself with what she falls in love with, so please do query her even if your manuscript falls outside these guidelines!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent is open to exceptions; a strong submission can succeed even if it doesn't match the listed preferences exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be emailed to hjacobson@icmpartners.com. Please send her your pitch and the first ten pages of your manuscript in the body of an email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required materials: a pitch (query) and the first ten pages pasted into the email body (not as attachments). Use the provided email address exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response practice / timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: I respond to every query, hopefully within about a month or so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent promises to reply to all queries and estimates response time around one month; set expectations accordingly when following up.
